findings.message: The new code calls `deploy_release_run` with no arguments; the deploy-release plugin (`plugins/tool/deploy-release/plugin.sh` lines 22-35) treats a missing `state_file` arg as a hard error, writes `verdict=error/disposition=broken` to ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR, and returns 1 — which the deploy plugin catches and overwrites with `disposition=unavailable` — making every real (non-dry-run) production deploy permanently fail at this call site.

deploy-release derives its own `artifacts_dir` from `dirname "$state_file"` (line 37-38), so even if the calling convention were fixed to pass a dummy state_file, the artifacts_dir used by deploy-release would diverge from `ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` used by the deploy plugin, meaning the two plugins would write to different paths and the deploy plugin's success-path result could silently miss the release artefacts.

When ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR is unset, `deploy_agent_run` returns 1 immediately without writing any result file; the engine receives a missing result rather than a structured `verdict=error` envelope, which may route through a different (potentially unguarded) engine failure path than the one the v2 contract expects.

Tests mock `deploy_release_run` via `_ZBUILD_DEPLOY_RELEASE_LOADED=1` for every run-path test (SPEC-2, SPEC-14, SPEC-20), so the actual interface between deploy and deploy-release is never exercised; the test suite gives a green result for a production-breaking interface mismatch because the mock returns 0 unconditionally rather than validating the call signature.

`_deploy_write_result` pipes `jq -n ...` into `atomic_write` without a `# sigpipe-ok` annotation; the CLAUDE.md SIGPIPE rule prohibits unannotated pipes in `plugins/` — if `atomic_write` exits early for any reason (e.g. ENOSPC), jq receives SIGPIPE and exits non-zero, causing `_deploy_write_result` to return non-zero under `set -euo pipefail` without having written the result file, leaving the engine with no artifact.

`_make_state` exports `ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS` and `ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` into the calling shell (by design), so every test that runs after a `_make_state` call inherits those paths; a future test inserted between two existing tests without its own `_make_state` call will silently use the previous test's artifact directory and produce false-green assertions.
